title: What is the ratio of grey to coloured bricks in a wall?
description: Grey and coloured bricks are counted over one whole block of each wall pattern, and the two counts are written as a ratio in the simplest form. The pattern repeats, so one block gives the ratio of the whole wall.
teaching_notes: One idea: count every row of one block before writing the ratio. Watch for students who count only the top row.

source: Figure it Out (ratios and proportions, question 6)
video_script.why: The child counts a whole block of a pattern and reduces the ratio of grey to coloured bricks to the simplest form.
video_script.substitution: Add the grey bricks and the coloured bricks over the block, then divide both by their highest common factor.
video_script.anchor: two brick walls with grey and coloured bricks, one repeating block marked on each
video_script.payoff_line: The first wall is three to two, and the second wall is four to three.

final_answer.spoken: the first wall is nine to six, which is three to two, and the second wall is sixteen to twelve, which is four to three

maths_rules: wall (a), one block, three rows: grey 2 + 3 + 4 = 9; coloured 3 + 2 + 1 = 6; ratio 9 : 6
HCF of 9 and 6 is 3; 9 ÷ 3 = 3 and 6 ÷ 3 = 2; simplest form 3 : 2
wall (b), one block: grey 16, coloured 12; ratio 16 : 12
HCF of 16 and 12 is 4; 16 ÷ 4 = 4 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3; simplest form 4 : 3
check: 3 × 3 = 9 and 3 × 2 = 6; 4 × 4 = 16 and 4 × 3 = 12; the pattern repeats, so the whole wall has the ratio of one block
video_script.design: One idea: count a whole block, then reduce. Uses the simplest form test of the solved example. The two walls stay for the whole video.
open_questions: The book gives the walls only as figures. The row counts used here (wall (a) grey 2, 3, 4 and coloured 3, 2, 1; wall (b) 16 grey and 12 coloured) come from the worklist and must match the printed figure.

<bookmark mark='pat'/>Grey and coloured bricks make a pattern that repeats along each wall.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What is the ratio of grey bricks to coloured bricks in each wall?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one outlined block of a wall; grey and coloured counts lifted out as grey : coloured; an arrow ÷ highest common factor giving the simplest form

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We use the same way as the example in your book. The pattern repeats, so one block gives the ratio of the whole wall.
<bookmark mark='count'/>Count the grey bricks and the coloured bricks in every row of the block.
<bookmark mark='simple'/>Then divide both numbers by their highest common factor. The ratio we get is called its simplest form.

beats.on_screen: Given: wall (a) block: grey 2, 3, 4 and coloured 3, 2, 1 in its three rows. Wall (b) block: 16 grey, 12 coloured

marks.a: wall (a) is written with its three rows
marks.b: wall (b) is written with 16 grey and 12 coloured

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Given, one block of the first wall has three rows.
<bookmark mark='g'/>The rows have two, three and four grey bricks.
<bookmark mark='c'/>They have three, two and one coloured bricks.
<bookmark mark='b'/>One block of the second wall has sixteen grey and twelve coloured bricks.

beats.on_screen: To find: grey : coloured for each wall, in simplest form

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the ratio of grey to coloured bricks for each wall, in simplest form.

marks.g: 2 + 3 + 4 = 9 is written and the nine grey bricks glow

narration: <bookmark mark='h'/>Step one, add the grey bricks of the first wall.
<bookmark mark='g'/>Two plus three plus four is nine.

marks.h: the coloured bricks of the block are outlined
marks.c: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 is written and the six coloured bricks glow

narration: <bookmark mark='h'/>Step two, add the coloured bricks of the same block.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Three plus two plus one is six.

marks.h: HCF is 3 is written beside it
marks.s: 9 ÷ 3 = 3 and 6 ÷ 3 = 2 are written and 3 : 2 is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='r'/>Step three, the ratio is nine to six.
<bookmark mark='h'/>The highest common factor is three.
<bookmark mark='s'/>Dividing both terms by three gives three to two.

marks.h: HCF is 4 is written beside it
marks.s: 16 ÷ 4 = 4 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3 are written and 4 : 3 is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='r'/>Step four, the second wall has sixteen to twelve.
<bookmark mark='h'/>The highest common factor is four.
<bookmark mark='s'/>Dividing both terms by four gives four to three.

marks.chk: the words Check: multiply back are written

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step five, check by multiplying back.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Three times three is nine, and three times two is six.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Four times four is sixteen, and four times three is twelve.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The first wall is three to two, and the second wall is four to three.
